request.previous_summary: Cycle 3 candidate 4424d5b… (OOF stacking of diverse log1p-target regressors with constrained meta-combiner, per-target OOF calibration, nonnegative clipping) ran end-to-end on public dev attempt 1: status ok, fidelity dev, seed 7, split dev, dev/score=-0.06923789562427363, cost ~5.44s/1 eval; no artifacts, partial curves, private metrics, or uncertainty. This is only marginally less negative than the prior target-specific HistGradientBoosting log1p attempt (-0.07289218173993534) and slightly better than earlier blends (-0.07775682882719075 and -0.08071985133840615), but with single-seed/single-split evidence and no baseline control it is not meaningful support. The stacking hypothesis remains plausible in design but unproven; the pipeline did not demonstrate a generalization gain. Retained limitations/failures: OOF meta-combiner may overfit correlated base learners or small fold grids; per-target calibration on the same OOF predictions risks leakage and may amplify near-zero bias; nonnegative clipping treats symptoms rather than bias source; physical aggregate features may discard fine-grained signal; only one seed and one dev split give no variance estimate or ablation; no artifact, per-target breakdown, non-stacked strong single-model control, or nested OOF evidence. Next steps: add a non-stacked strong single-model control; ablate calibration and clipping independently from stacking; increase seeds/folds and report seed variance; constrain meta-learner more aggressively (nonnegative simplex weights, shrinkage toward best base learner, simple ridge/mean blend) with nested OOF; inspect per-target residuals to verify near-zero bias correction. Do not claim generalization improvement until multi-seed, ablated dev evidence supports it. child_insight.summary: Cycle 4 candidate ea3c337c… tested replacing one-hot/frequency spacegroup handling and learned stacking with smoothed out-of-fold spacegroup target encoding plus composition/lattice aggregate features, a tuned HistGradientBoosting regressor on log1p targets, and an optional fixed HGB+ExtraTrees blend selected by nested grouped OOF validation; folds grouped by spacegroup and composition motif. New public dev evidence: attempt 1 status ok, fidelity dev, seed [7], split dev, dev/score = -0.07072699042464957, ~8.50s, 1 eval; no artifacts, no partial curves, no private metrics, no per-target breakdown, no uncertainty, generic feedback only: “Public training validation completed. Improve generalization; output a complete Python program.” Interpretation: pipeline ran end-to-end but the only public dev score is negative and slightly worse than the prior stacking attempt (-0.06923789562427363); this does not validate the hypothesis and gives no evidence that target encoding plus optional ET blending improves generalization. Added complexity is not justified by current evidence. Relative to earlier log1p HGB/stacking attempts (e.g. -0.07289218173993534 and -0.06923789562427363), all remain below zero and differences are too small to interpret without multi-seed/split variance, ablation, or a strong non-encoded single-model control. Retained limitations/failures: single dev split and seed limit reliability; negative score may reflect underfitting, overfitting, fold-induced distribution shift, poor metric alignment after log1p back-transform, or model capacity/feature issues; smoothed out-of-fold spacegroup target encoding can still leak or overfit rare spacegroups, especially when grouping by spacegroup and composition motif creates sparse groups or separates similar crystal families; nested OOF blend selection can overfit validation structure; fixed HGB+ET averaging may not capture crystallographic invariance or lattice/composition interactions; no learning curves, failure trace, per-target breakdown, or ablation isolating encoding vs grouping vs HGB tuning vs ET blend is available. Next interpretation should simplify and ablate: compare no target encoding vs regularized/shrunk target encoding, test aggregate-only features, verify grouped folds and rare-group handling, tune HGB independently, evaluate a no-blend baseline before any ET averaging, add a strong non-encoded single-model control, increase seeds/folds and report variance, and return a complete Python program aimed at better public generalization. Do not claim generalization improvement until multi-seed, ablated dev evidence supports it.
